hook: A permission ladder — graduated levels of autonomy from review-every-action to approve-everything — is how a harness governs what an autonomous agent may do without asking. Claude Code, this lesson's worked example, exposes six such modes: "plan" asks before every action, "default" (labeled "Manual" in the UI) asks only for risky ones, "acceptEdits" auto-approves file writes but still confirms shell execution, and "bypassPermissions" approves everything. Auto Mode — the `auto` permission mode — replaces per-action approval with a separate classifier model that reviews each action before it runs and blocks anything that escalates beyond what the request asked for. Action budgets are enforced via `max_turns` and `max_budget_usd`. Availability of `auto` depends on plan, org enablement, model, and provider — and Anthropic is explicit that the classifier is not sufficient alone.
